newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan bars ousted PM Bhutto from seeing husband.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan bars ousted PM Bhutto from seeing husband.

text.p: Pakistani authorities have refused to allow ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto to visit her husband, detained since the government was sacked five days ago, Bhutto's spokesman said on Sunday.
Bhutto last saw Asif Ali Zardari on Thursday, two days after she was ousted over disputed charges of corruption and misrule and he was picked up by soldiers, spokesman Shah Mahmood Qureshi said.

Qureshi, former state minister for parliamentary affairs, said authorities holding Zardari in an official residence near the capital Islamabad had turned down Bhutto's requests since Thursday to see him.
"She has not been permitted yet to see him again," Qureshi told Reuters, saying the residence had been declared an ad hoc jail. "They have given no solid reason."
Government officials were not available for comment.
Authorities had told Bhutto after Zardari was detained that she would be allowed to visit him twice a week, and on Saturday told her she could see him once every two weeks, Qureshi said.
Bhutto was permitted to see Zardari last Thursday, hours after she threatened to bring kidnapping charges against President Farooq Leghari, who sacked her three-year government.

Zardari was picked up by soldiers in Lahore last Tuesday and later transferred to the residence. Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's government first said Zardari was in "protective custody" and an investigation was perhaps under way.
Later authorities said he was being held without charge under a law for the maintenance of public order.

Zardari is the target of corruption allegations levelled against Bhutto's government and has also been accused of conspiring to murder Bhutto's brother Murtaza, killed by police in Karachi on September 20. Zardari has denied the charges.

The murder case took another twist on Saturday when supporters of Murtaza filed a formal complaint in the financial capital Karachi accusing unnamed officials in Bhutto's government of conspiring to kill him.
Bhutto planned to write to the Interior Ministry and local authorities requesting a meeting with Zardari and demanding that he be released unless charges were filed, Qureshi said.

"They have to release him if there are no charges," the spokesman said. "We have no idea why he is being held. If there were going to be charges, they would have been levelled by now. After five days, it could be that they are fabricating some."
After Bhutto saw Zardari last week, she said he was in good physical condition.
Last week Bhutto said she intended this week to challenge Leghari's order sacking her. Qureshi said the challenge would be filed as soon as lawyers finished drafting it.

Bhutto was confined by authorities to the prime minister's official residence for some 36 hours after being sacked. Later, restrictions on her movement were lifted but authorities continue to control the flow of political supporters and former ministers into the residence, Qureshi said.

Bhutto intended to move out of the official residence and into her private home in Islamabad either on Monday or Tuesday, he said. She also planned to go soon to Karachi, where she has another home, to move personal effects and meet supporters.
